items.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The big tenor player around town then was Joshua Jackson... We all used to watch him

ctx.x: Jimmy Ellis had some place that they were jamming at when I was here, that was similar to that.

He was down at 53rd Street, back in the alley, yeah. But see Jimmy, this is like a – almost a 50-year span. I’m talking about when I – before I went into the Army. It’s around the last of the ’30s and a couple years into the ’40s. Lank Keyes was holding these sets. The big tenor player around town then was Joshua Jackson. He went to DuSable, real light-skinned cat, very, very fair. He had all this technique. We all used to watch him, because he could hit high F and all this. He was an excellent reader.
I can remember Lank Keyes playing and rehearsing this tune maybe three years. [Freeman sings.] What’s the name of that?
